structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, sex-specific growth-velocity curves for stature across ages 6-18 have similar shape, with the girls' adolescent acceleration beginning and peaking about 1-3 years earlier than the boys', and the two curves differ in amplitude.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using survey-weighted median measured stature by single year of age (or by age in months) and sex, compute velocity as the annual increment and smooth it. All three conditions must hold. (1) The age of peak velocity is earlier in girls than in boys by at least 1.0 year, with a 95% bootstrap CI (survey-cycle resampling) that excludes 0. (2) The age at which velocity first rises above its pre-pubertal minimum is also earlier in girls by at least 0.5 year. (3) After shifting the girls' curve in time by the best lag, the Pearson correlation between the two velocity curves is at least 0.85, with the best lag between 1 and 3 years. Amplitude must also differ: peak velocities must differ by a ratio that departs from 1.00 by at least 5%, with a CI that excludes 1.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if any of the following holds. (a) The girls' peak velocity age is not earlier than the boys' by at least 0.5 year, or the CI includes 0. (b) The best-lag correlation between the two velocity curves is below 0.70, so the shapes are not similar. (c) The best lag is below 0.5 year or above 4 years. Results that fall between the pass and fail thresholds are reported as inconclusive.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'curve of growth velocity' is the annual increment in stature (cm/year) against age. 'Phase' is the timing of the adolescent acceleration, measured by the take-off age and the peak-velocity age. 'Amplitude' is the height of the peak velocity. 'Very similar' is operationalised as high correlation of the two curves after a time shift. Modern reinterpretation: NHANES is cross-sectional, so velocity is estimated from differences in age-specific median stature between successive ages. This is a population-level approximation of individual longitudinal velocity and tends to blur peaks. The test therefore uses pooled cycles, smoothing, and bootstrap CIs, and it applies the same procedure to both sexes. Measured stature from the examination body-measures files is used, not self-reported stature.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) – Body Measures (BMX) examination data
dataset.publisher: US CDC National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS)
dataset.why_it_fits: NHANES records measured standing height (BMXHT) in the examination body-measures files. The demographics files give age in years (RIDAGEYR) and months (RIDAGEEX) and sex (RIAGENDR). The survey weights (WTMEC2YR) are also provided. Pooling cycles gives enough children aged 6-18 to estimate weighted median stature by age and sex, from which velocity curves can be derived and compared. All files are freely downloadable as SAS transport files.
